raw_response:
I’m 65 now, so I don’t chase fancy things. I do mostly what has worked on my land and what I see in the village. With only 2 people at home, I can’t spread myself too thin, so I’ll keep most of the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece in cotton. Wheat and maize are the steady income, and cotton is there so if one side is weak, I still have something else. Fertilizer is expensive, water costs money too, so I won’t push too hard, but I also don’t dare cut too much because if the crop turns yellow or thin, the loss is bigger than the savings.

For the wheat land, I’ll manage it much like last year: one base fertilizer, then one topdress around jointing, and irrigate when the crop really needs it. After wheat harvest, I’ll rush to plant summer maize right away, because if you miss those few days, yield drops fast. Cotton I’ll keep on the smaller plot because it takes more watching and hand work, and with only 2 people I can’t do too much of it. I’ll use round amounts, about what my neighbors use, not exact calculations.
